title: A Day at the Fire Station
photo: Firefighters fire station / Fire truck firefighters training / Firefighter turnout gear
p: Maria is a firefighter in a small American town.
玛丽亚是美国一个小镇上的消防员。
She works at the fire station for twenty-four hours and then goes home for two days.
她在消防站连续工作二十四小时，然后回家休息两天。
The firefighters eat, sleep and cook together at the station, like a big family.
消防员们在消防站一起吃饭、睡觉、做饭，就像一个大家庭。
Every morning, Maria checks the fire truck, the hoses and her heavy coat and helmet.
每天早上，玛丽亚都会检查消防车、水管以及她厚重的外套和头盔。
When the alarm rings, she must be ready to leave in about a minute.
警报一响，她必须在大约一分钟内准备好出发。
Fighting fires is only part of her job.
灭火只是她工作的一部分。
She also helps people after car accidents and teaches children what to do if there is a fire at home.
她还在车祸后帮助伤者，并教孩子们家里着火时该怎么做。
q: How long does Maria work at one time?
What does Maria check every morning?
The truck, the hoses and her coat and helmet
Which is also part of Maria's job?

title: The Zookeeper
photo: Zookeeper feeding animals / Zoo keeper elephant / Zookeeper giraffe feeding
p: Tom is a zookeeper, and his day starts at seven in the morning, before the visitors arrive.
汤姆是一名动物园饲养员，他的一天从早上七点开始，那时游客还没来。
First, he cleans the animals' homes and gives them fresh water.
首先，他打扫动物的住处，给它们换上新鲜的水。
Then he prepares their food.
然后他准备它们的食物。
The giraffes eat leaves, and the penguins eat fish.
长颈鹿吃树叶，企鹅吃鱼。
Tom watches the animals carefully every day.
汤姆每天都仔细观察动物。
If an animal does not eat or moves slowly, it may be sick, so he calls the zoo's doctor.
如果某只动物不吃东西或者行动迟缓，它可能生病了，于是他会给动物园的兽医打电话。
He also gives the animals toys and puzzles so they do not get bored.
他还给动物们玩具和益智游戏，免得它们感到无聊。
Tom says the best part of his job is getting to know each animal's personality.
汤姆说，他工作中最棒的部分是了解每只动物的个性。
q: What does Tom do if an animal does not eat?
He moves it to another zoo
Why does Tom give the animals toys?
So they do not get bored

title: Two Minutes, Twice a Day
photo: Child brushing teeth / Toothbrush and toothpaste / Dentist examining teeth
p: Dentists say we should brush our teeth twice a day, for about two minutes each time.
牙医说，我们应该每天刷两次牙，每次大约两分钟。
Two minutes may sound short, but many people stop after only thirty or forty seconds.
两分钟听起来不长，但很多人只刷三四十秒就停下了。
Some electric toothbrushes have a timer to help.
有些电动牙刷带有计时器来帮忙。
Brushing is important because tiny bacteria live in our mouths.
刷牙很重要，因为我们的嘴里生活着微小的细菌。
They feed on sugar and make acid, and the acid can make holes in our teeth.
它们以糖为食并产生酸，而酸会在牙齿上腐蚀出洞来。
Toothpaste with fluoride helps keep teeth strong.
含氟牙膏有助于保持牙齿坚固。
It is also a good idea to visit a dentist for a checkup, even when nothing hurts.
即使牙不疼，去看牙医做个检查也是个好主意。
q: How long should we brush our teeth each time?
What makes holes in our teeth?
When should we visit a dentist?

title: Why We Need Sleep
photo: Teenager sleeping in bed / Sleeping student / Alarm clock bedroom
p: We spend about one third of our lives asleep.
我们一生中大约有三分之一的时间在睡觉。
Sleep is not a waste of time.
睡觉并不是浪费时间。
While we sleep, our body repairs itself and our brain stores what we learned during the day.
我们睡觉时，身体会自我修复，大脑会储存白天学到的东西。
Teenagers usually need more sleep than adults, often eight to ten hours a night.
青少年通常比成年人需要更多睡眠，一般每晚八到十个小时。
But many students go to bed late because they are looking at their phones.
但很多学生睡得很晚，因为他们在看手机。
The bright screen can make it harder to fall asleep.
明亮的屏幕会让人更难入睡。
Doctors suggest putting the phone away before bed and going to sleep at the same time every night.
医生建议睡前把手机收起来，并且每晚在同一时间睡觉。
q: What does the brain do while we sleep?
It watches dreams on a screen
How much sleep do teenagers often need?
Putting the phone away before bed
Going to bed at different times
Looking at a screen to relax

title: Which Bin Does It Go In?
photo: Recycling bins sorting / Curbside recycling bin / Recycling plastic bottles
p: In many towns in the United States and the UK, families have more than one trash bin.
在美国和英国的许多城镇，每个家庭都有不止一个垃圾桶。
One is for trash, and another is for things that can be recycled, like paper, cans and some plastic bottles.
一个装普通垃圾，另一个装可回收的东西，比如纸、易拉罐和一些塑料瓶。
Some places also have a bin for food waste.
有些地方还有专门装厨余垃圾的桶。
Recycling saves materials and energy.
回收可以节约材料和能源。
For example, an old can may become part of a new can or even a bike.
比如，一个旧易拉罐可能会成为新易拉罐的一部分，甚至变成一辆自行车。
But recycling only works if people put the right things in the right bin.
但只有人们把正确的东西放进正确的桶里，回收才能起作用。
A greasy pizza box or a dirty bottle can spoil a whole load of paper or plastic, so it is best to empty and rinse containers first.
一个沾满油的披萨盒或一个脏瓶子就可能毁掉整整一车纸或塑料，所以最好先把容器倒空并冲洗干净。
q: Which of these can usually be recycled?
Food waste in the recycling bin
What can an old can become?
Part of a new can or a bike
What should you do before recycling a bottle?

title: The Animal Doctor
photo: Veterinarian examining dog / Vet clinic cat examination / Veterinary surgery
p: Dr. Lee is a veterinarian, or "vet," in a busy city clinic.
李医生是一名兽医，在城里一家繁忙的诊所工作。
Most of her patients are dogs and cats, but sometimes people bring rabbits, birds or even snakes.
她的病人大多是猫和狗，但有时人们也会带来兔子、鸟甚至蛇。
Her job is hard because animals cannot say where it hurts.
她的工作很难，因为动物说不出哪里疼。
She has to look, listen and ask the owners many questions.
她必须观察、倾听，并向主人问很多问题。
Is the dog eating?
狗吃东西吗？
Is the cat drinking more water than usual?
猫是不是比平时喝水更多？
She also gives young animals vaccines to protect them from dangerous diseases.
她还给幼小的动物接种疫苗，保护它们免受危险疾病的侵害。
Dr. Lee says the happiest moment is when a sick pet goes home healthy with its family.
李医生说，最开心的时刻就是生病的宠物恢复健康、和家人一起回家的时候。
q: Why is Dr. Lee's job hard?
Animals cannot say where it hurts
Who does Dr. Lee ask questions?

title: Behind the Wheel of a City Bus
photo: City bus driver / Public transit bus interior / Bus stop passengers boarding
p: Every weekday, Sam drives a city bus along the same route.
每个工作日，萨姆都沿着同一条路线开城市公交车。
His first trip starts at 5:30 a.m., when the streets are still dark and quiet.
他的第一趟车早上五点半出发，那时街道上还又黑又安静。
Many of his early passengers are nurses, cleaners and bakers going to work.
他早班车上的许多乘客是去上班的护士、清洁工和面包师。
Sam must keep to a timetable, but safety always comes first.
萨姆必须遵守时刻表，但安全永远是第一位的。
He waits for older people to sit down before he moves.
他会等老人坐好后才开车。
He also lowers the bus so that people in wheelchairs can get on easily.
他还会把车身降低，让坐轮椅的人能轻松上车。
After many years, Sam knows many passengers by name, and they often say "Thank you" when they get off.
多年下来，萨姆能叫出很多乘客的名字，他们下车时也常说“谢谢”。
q: When does Sam's first trip start?
What does Sam do for people in wheelchairs?
What is most important to Sam?

title: The Little Robot That Cleans
photo: Robot vacuum cleaner / Robotic vacuum on floor / Roomba
p: Many homes now have a robot vacuum.
如今很多家庭都有扫地机器人。
It is round and flat, so it can go under beds and sofas.
它又圆又扁，所以能钻到床和沙发底下。
It moves around the room by itself and picks up dust and crumbs.
它在房间里自己移动，吸起灰尘和碎屑。
The robot has sensors that help it find walls and stairs, so it does not fall down.
机器人装有传感器，帮助它发现墙壁和楼梯，这样就不会摔下去。
Some robots also make a map of the home.
有些机器人还会绘制家里的地图。
When the battery is low, the robot goes back to its base to charge.
电量不足时，机器人会回到底座充电。
However, it is not perfect.
不过，它并不完美。
Socks, cables and toys on the floor can stop it, so people still need to tidy up first!
地上的袜子、电线和玩具会把它卡住，所以人们还是得先收拾一下！
q: Why can the robot go under beds?
What does the robot do when its battery is low?
It goes back to its base
It stops in the middle of the room
Socks and cables on the floor

title: Saving in a Jar
photo: Coins in a glass jar / Piggy bank coins / Child saving money
p: When Emma was eight, her parents gave her a small allowance every week.
艾玛八岁时，父母每周给她一点零花钱。
They also gave her three glass jars with labels: Spend, Save and Share.
他们还给了她三个贴着标签的玻璃罐：“花”“存”“分享”。
Every week, Emma divided her money among the jars.
每周，艾玛都把钱分到这几个罐子里。
She used the Spend jar for snacks and stickers.
“花”罐里的钱她用来买零食和贴纸。
The Save jar was for a new bike, so it filled up slowly.
“存”罐是为了买新自行车，所以装满得很慢。
The Share jar was for giving to an animal shelter.
“分享”罐里的钱是捐给动物收容所的。
It took Emma almost a year to buy the bike, but she felt very proud.
艾玛花了将近一年才买到自行车，但她感到非常自豪。
She learned that waiting for something can make it feel even more special.
她明白了，等待一样东西会让它显得更加珍贵。
q: How many jars did Emma have?
What was the Save jar for?
Waiting can make something feel more special

title: Up Before the Sun: A Dairy Farmer
photo: Dairy cows milking parlor / Dairy farm cows barn / Holstein cows farm
p: Jack is a dairy farmer, and his cows do not take a day off.
杰克是一名奶农，他的奶牛可从来不休息。
They need to be milked twice a day, every day of the year, even on holidays.
它们一年到头每天都要挤两次奶，节假日也不例外。
So Jack gets up at four o'clock in the morning.
所以杰克凌晨四点就起床。
Today, machines do the milking, but Jack still checks each cow.
如今挤奶由机器完成，但杰克仍然要检查每一头牛。
He makes sure they are healthy and have enough food and clean water.
他要确保它们身体健康，有足够的饲料和干净的水。
Each cow has a number tag on her ear, and some farmers use computers to follow how much milk each cow gives.
每头牛的耳朵上都有一个编号牌，有些农民还用电脑记录每头牛的产奶量。
A truck takes the milk to a factory, where it is made into milk, cheese and yogurt for the shops.
卡车把牛奶运到工厂，在那里加工成牛奶、奶酪和酸奶，送往商店。
q: How often are the cows milked?
What is on each cow's ear?

title: Eyes on the Sky
zh: 天空的守望者：空中交通管制员
photo: Air traffic control tower / Air traffic controllers radar room / Airport control tower interior
p: High in a glass tower at a busy airport, Rachel watches dozens of planes take off and land.
在一个繁忙机场的玻璃塔台高处，雷切尔注视着几十架飞机起飞和降落。
She is an air traffic controller, and her job is to keep aircraft at a safe distance from one another.
她是一名空中交通管制员，她的工作是让飞机彼此之间保持安全距离。
Using radar screens and radio, she gives pilots instructions about when to land, which runway to use and how high to fly.
她借助雷达屏幕和无线电，指示飞行员何时降落、使用哪条跑道以及飞多高。
Every instruction must be clear and short, and pilots repeat it back to confirm they have understood.
每一条指令都必须简短明确，飞行员会复述一遍以确认自己听懂了。
To avoid confusion, controllers around the world use English and say numbers in a special way, such as "niner" for nine.
为了避免混淆，世界各地的管制员都使用英语，并用特殊的方式说数字，比如把九说成“niner”。
Because the work requires intense concentration, controllers take regular breaks during their shifts.
由于这项工作需要高度集中注意力，管制员在值班期间会定时休息。
Rachel admits the pressure is high, but she enjoys solving a new puzzle every few minutes.
雷切尔承认压力很大，但她享受每隔几分钟就解开一个新难题的感觉。
q: What is the main purpose of Rachel's job?
To keep aircraft at a safe distance from one another
Why do pilots repeat instructions back?
To ask for a different runway
Why do controllers take regular breaks?
They have very little to do

title: The Power of a Short Nap
photo: Office worker napping at desk / Power nap / Person sleeping on couch afternoon
p: Many people feel sleepy in the early afternoon, especially after lunch.
很多人在午后，尤其是午饭后会感到困倦。
This "afternoon dip" is a natural part of the body clock, not just the result of a heavy meal.
这种“午后低谷”是生物钟的自然组成部分，而不只是饱餐一顿的结果。
In some cultures, a midday rest has long been part of daily life.
在一些文化中，午间休息早已是日常生活的一部分。
Sleep researchers have found that a short nap of about ten to twenty minutes can improve alertness and mood.
睡眠研究者发现，大约十到二十分钟的短暂小睡可以提高警觉性、改善情绪。
The key is to wake up before the brain enters deep sleep.
关键是要在大脑进入深度睡眠之前醒来。
If a nap lasts too long, people may wake up feeling groggy, a state known as "sleep inertia."
如果小睡时间过长，人醒来时可能会昏昏沉沉，这种状态被称为“睡眠惯性”。
Napping late in the day can also make it harder to fall asleep at night.
傍晚小睡还可能让人晚上更难入睡。
For most people, then, the ideal nap is short and taken in the early afternoon.
因此，对大多数人来说，理想的小睡应该时间短，并且安排在午后早些时候。
q: According to the passage, what causes the "afternoon dip"?
How long is a good short nap?
About an hour and a half
Feeling groggy after waking from a long nap

title: The Marshmallow Test
photo: Marshmallows on a plate / Child looking at marshmallow / Stanford University campus
p: In the late 1960s and early 1970s, psychologist Walter Mischel and his team at Stanford University gave young children a simple choice.
二十世纪六十年代末到七十年代初，心理学家沃尔特·米歇尔和他在斯坦福大学的团队给年幼的孩子们出了一道简单的选择题。
A child could eat one treat, such as a marshmallow, right away, or wait alone for several minutes and get two.
孩子可以马上吃掉一块零食，比如一颗棉花糖，也可以独自等上几分钟，然后得到两颗。
Some children ate the treat immediately, while others covered their eyes, sang songs or turned away to resist temptation.
有些孩子立刻就吃了，另一些则捂住眼睛、唱歌或者转过身去抵抗诱惑。
Years later, follow-up studies suggested that children who waited longer tended to do better at school.
多年后，追踪研究表明，等待时间较长的孩子往往学习成绩更好。
The test became famous as a measure of self-control.
这个实验作为衡量自控力的方法而出名。
However, more recent research with larger and more varied groups of children found that the link was weaker than first thought.
然而，近来以规模更大、背景更多样的儿童为对象的研究发现，这种关联比最初认为的要弱。
Family background, such as whether a child could trust that adults would keep their promises, also seemed to matter.
家庭背景，比如孩子是否相信大人会信守承诺，似乎也有影响。
The lesson may be that waiting is not only about willpower but also about circumstances.
也许这告诉我们，等待不仅关乎意志力，也关乎所处的环境。
q: What choice did the children have?
Eat one treat now or wait for two
Eat a treat or play a game
Sing a song or go home
Choose between a marshmallow and a cookie
What did more recent research find?
The link with school success was weaker than first thought
Waiting has no connection with anything
Children today cannot wait at all
What does the passage suggest about waiting?
It depends on both willpower and circumstances
It matters only for young children

title: Why We Put Things Off
photo: Student procrastinating at desk / Cluttered desk with laptop / To-do list notebook
p: Almost everyone has delayed an important task while doing something less useful, like cleaning a drawer or scrolling through videos.
几乎每个人都有过把重要任务往后推、转而去做些不那么有用的事情的经历，比如整理抽屉或刷视频。
This habit is called procrastination, and it is often blamed on laziness.
这种习惯被称为拖延，人们常常把它归咎于懒惰。
Many psychologists, however, see it differently.
然而，许多心理学家有不同的看法。
They argue that procrastination is often a way of avoiding unpleasant feelings.
他们认为，拖延往往是一种逃避不愉快情绪的方式。
A task may feel boring, confusing or frightening because we fear we will do it badly.
一项任务可能让人觉得无聊、困惑或可怕，因为我们担心自己会做不好。
Putting it off brings quick relief, but the stress returns later, usually stronger.
拖延能带来短暂的解脱，但压力过后会卷土重来，而且通常更强烈。
Some simple strategies can help.
一些简单的策略会有帮助。
Breaking a big job into small steps makes it less frightening, and promising yourself to work for just five minutes often makes starting easier.
把一项大工作分解成小步骤，会让它不那么可怕；而答应自己只干五分钟，往往能让开始变得更容易。
Being kind to yourself after a delay, rather than feeling guilty, may also reduce the chance of delaying again.
拖延之后善待自己而不是感到内疚，也可能减少再次拖延的几率。
q: According to many psychologists, what is procrastination often about?
What happens after putting a task off?
We feel relaxed for a long time
Which strategy is mentioned in the passage?
Breaking a big job into small steps

title: Tomatoes and Timers
zh: 番茄与计时器：番茄工作法
photo: Tomato kitchen timer / Pomodoro timer / Studying with timer
p: In the late 1980s, an Italian university student named Francesco Cirillo was struggling to focus on his studies.
二十世纪八十年代末，一位名叫弗朗切斯科·西里洛的意大利大学生在学习时很难集中注意力。
He picked up a kitchen timer shaped like a tomato and challenged himself to work without stopping until it rang.
他拿起一个番茄形状的厨房计时器，挑战自己在铃响之前一直不停地学习。
Since "pomodoro" means tomato in Italian, his method became known as the Pomodoro Technique.
由于“pomodoro”在意大利语里是番茄的意思，他的方法便被称为“番茄工作法”。
The basic idea is simple.
基本思路很简单。
You choose one task, set a timer for twenty-five minutes and work on nothing else.
你选定一项任务，设定二十五分钟的计时，期间只做这一件事。
When the timer rings, you take a short break of about five minutes, and after four rounds you take a longer one.
计时器响了，你就休息大约五分钟；完成四轮之后，再休息更长时间。
If you remember something else you need to do, you write it down and return to it later.
如果你想起别的需要做的事，就把它记下来，稍后再处理。
Supporters say the method turns a huge task into manageable pieces and makes breaks a reward rather than a distraction.
支持者说，这种方法把庞大的任务变成了可以掌控的小块，并让休息成为一种奖励而不是干扰。
q: It was invented by a farmer
How long is one work period in the method?
What should you do if you remember another task?
Write it down and return to it later

title: Working at Height: The Wind Turbine Technician
zh: 高空作业：风力发电机技术员
photo: Wind turbine technician climbing / Wind turbine maintenance nacelle / Wind farm turbines
p: Some people go up a few floors in an elevator to get to work.
有些人坐电梯上几层楼去上班。
Carlos climbs a ladder inside a wind turbine that is taller than a thirty-story building.
卡洛斯则要在一座比三十层楼还高的风力发电机内部爬梯子。
He is a wind turbine technician, one of the jobs created by the growth of renewable energy.
他是一名风力发电机技术员，这是随着可再生能源发展而出现的职业之一。
At the top, inside a compartment called the nacelle, he inspects the gearbox, the generator and the system that turns the blades toward the wind.
在顶部一个叫做机舱的隔间里，他检查齿轮箱、发电机以及让叶片转向迎风方向的系统。
Regular maintenance prevents small faults from turning into expensive breakdowns.
定期维护可以防止小故障演变成代价高昂的大损坏。
Safety rules are strict: technicians wear harnesses, work in pairs and never climb in strong winds or thunderstorms.
安全规定很严格：技术员要系安全带、两人一组工作，并且从不在大风或雷雨天攀爬。
The job requires both technical skills and physical fitness.
这份工作既需要技术能力，也需要良好的体能。
For Carlos, the reward is the view and the knowledge that he is helping to produce clean electricity.
对卡洛斯来说，回报是那里的风景，以及知道自己正在帮助生产清洁电力。
q: Where does Carlos do much of his inspection work?
In the nacelle at the top
At the bottom of the sea
It prevents small faults from becoming expensive breakdowns
It lets technicians climb in storms
It turns the turbine off forever

title: Shrinkflation: Same Price, Less Inside
zh: 缩水式通胀：价格不变，分量变少
photo: Supermarket shelf snacks / Potato chip bags supermarket / Grocery shopping cart aisle
p: Have you ever opened a bag of chips and felt that there were fewer inside than before?
你有没有过这样的感觉：打开一袋薯片，觉得里面的量比以前少了？
You might be right.
你的感觉可能没错。
When their costs rise, some companies keep the price the same but quietly make the product smaller.
当成本上升时，有些公司保持价格不变，却悄悄把产品做小。
Economists call this "shrinkflation," a combination of "shrink" and "inflation."
经济学家称之为“缩水式通胀”，这是“缩水”和“通货膨胀”两个词的组合。
Companies do this because shoppers tend to notice a higher price much more quickly than a smaller package.
公司这样做，是因为购物者对涨价的察觉往往比对包装变小快得多。
A chocolate bar might lose a few grams, or a box of cereal might stay the same size on the outside while containing less.
一块巧克力可能少了几克，一盒麦片可能外观大小不变，里面却装得更少了。
The practice is generally legal as long as the correct weight is printed on the label.
只要标签上印着正确的重量，这种做法通常是合法的。
Consumer experts therefore advise shoppers to compare the "unit price," the cost per gram or per item, which many supermarkets display on the shelf.
因此，消费专家建议购物者比较“单价”，即每克或每件的价格，很多超市都会把它标在货架上。
q: Making a product smaller while keeping the price the same
Raising the price of a product
Why do companies prefer shrinkflation to raising prices?
Shoppers notice price increases more quickly
It is cheaper to print labels
What do experts advise shoppers to compare?

title: Phones Away at School?
photo: Students using smartphones classroom / Phone locker school / Teenagers with phones
p: In recent years, a growing number of schools and countries have introduced rules limiting the use of mobile phones during the school day.
近年来，越来越多的学校和国家出台规定，限制在校期间使用手机。
In some schools, students lock their phones in pouches or leave them in lockers until classes are over.
在一些学校，学生要把手机锁进专用袋里或放在储物柜里，直到放学。
Supporters believe that phones distract students from lessons and reduce face-to-face conversation during breaks.
支持者认为，手机会让学生在课堂上分心，并减少课间面对面的交流。
Teachers in schools with bans often report that playgrounds become noisier, in a good way, as students talk and play together.
实行禁令学校的老师常说，操场变得更热闹了，这是好事，因为学生们会一起聊天、玩耍。
They also hope that limiting phones will reduce online bullying.
他们还希望限制手机能减少网络欺凌。
Critics, however, point out that many parents want to contact their children in an emergency.
然而，批评者指出，很多家长希望在紧急情况下能联系上孩子。
Others argue that schools should teach young people to use technology responsibly instead of simply banning it.
还有人认为，学校应该教年轻人负责任地使用科技，而不是一禁了之。
Researchers are still studying how much difference such bans make to learning and well-being.
研究人员仍在研究此类禁令对学习和身心健康到底有多大影响。
q: What do teachers often notice in schools with phone bans?
Playgrounds become noisier as students talk and play
What is one argument against phone bans?
Parents want to contact children in an emergency
What is the current state of research on phone bans?
Researchers are still studying their effects

title: Beyond the Password
photo: Two-factor authentication smartphone / Password login screen / Security key USB
p: For decades, a password was the main thing protecting our email and bank accounts.
几十年来，密码一直是保护我们电子邮箱和银行账户的主要手段。
The problem is that passwords are easy to guess, steal or reuse.
问题在于，密码很容易被猜到、盗取或重复使用。
If you use the same password on many websites and one of them is hacked, criminals can try it everywhere.
如果你在很多网站上用同一个密码，而其中一个网站被黑客攻破，犯罪分子就可以拿它到处尝试。
That is why many services now offer two-factor authentication.
这就是为什么如今很多服务都提供双重认证。
After typing your password, you must prove your identity a second way, for example with a code sent to your phone or generated by an app.
输入密码后，你还必须用第二种方式证明身份，比如用发送到手机上的验证码或由应用程序生成的验证码。
Even if someone steals your password, they cannot log in without the second factor.
即使有人偷到了你的密码，没有第二重验证也无法登录。
Security experts also recommend using a password manager, which creates and remembers a long, unique password for every site.
安全专家还建议使用密码管理器，它会为每个网站生成并记住一个长而独特的密码。
Some companies are now moving toward "passkeys," which use your device and a fingerprint or face scan instead of a password.
一些公司正在转向“通行密钥”，用你的设备加上指纹或面部扫描来代替密码。
q: Why is reusing one password dangerous?
If one site is hacked, criminals can try it everywhere
You prove your identity a second way after the password
You call the bank every time
What does a password manager do?
Creates and remembers a unique password for every site
Removes the need for any security

title: Why Cities Feel Hotter
zh: 城市为什么更热：热岛效应
photo: Urban heat island / Green roof city / Street trees shade city sidewalk
p: On a summer evening, the center of a big city can be noticeably warmer than the countryside around it.
在夏日傍晚，大城市的中心可能比周围的乡村明显更热。
Scientists call this the "urban heat island" effect.
科学家把这称为“城市热岛”效应。
There are several reasons for it.
造成这种现象的原因有好几个。
Dark roads and roofs absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat slowly at night.
深色的道路和屋顶白天吸收阳光，夜里再慢慢把热量释放出来。
Cars, air conditioners and factories add even more heat.
汽车、空调和工厂又增加了更多热量。
Meanwhile, cities have fewer trees and plants, which cool the air by providing shade and releasing water vapor.
与此同时，城市里的树木和植物较少，而它们能通过提供阴凉和释放水蒸气来给空气降温。
The extra heat is not just uncomfortable; during heat waves it can be dangerous, especially for elderly people.
额外的热量不仅让人不舒服，在热浪期间还可能带来危险，尤其是对老年人。
To fight it, many cities are planting more street trees, building parks and encouraging "green roofs" covered with plants.
为了应对这一问题，许多城市正在种植更多行道树、修建公园，并鼓励建设覆盖植物的“绿色屋顶”。
Some are even painting roofs and pavements in light colors to reflect sunlight.
有些城市甚至把屋顶和路面刷成浅色来反射阳光。
q: What is the "urban heat island" effect?
City centers being warmer than the countryside around them
Summer being longer in the countryside
How do trees help cool the air?
By providing shade and releasing water vapor
Why are some cities painting roofs in light colors?
To help plants grow on them

title: Paid to Find Problems: The Game Tester
zh: 找问题也是工作：游戏测试员
photo: Video game tester / Gaming controller playing / Software testing computer screen
p: Many teenagers dream of being paid to play video games all day.
许多青少年梦想着整天玩电子游戏还能拿工资。
Game testers, also called quality assurance testers, do spend their working hours playing games, but the job is less glamorous than it sounds.
游戏测试员，也叫质量保证测试员，确实把工作时间都花在玩游戏上，但这份工作并不像听起来那么光鲜。
A tester's real task is to find bugs before the public does.
测试员真正的任务是赶在公众之前发现漏洞。
That might mean walking into the same wall a hundred times to check whether the character falls through it.
这可能意味着让角色撞同一堵墙一百次，看看他会不会穿墙掉下去。
It might also mean pressing buttons in strange orders or playing the same level for days.
也可能意味着按奇怪的顺序按键，或者连续好几天玩同一个关卡。
Every time something goes wrong, the tester writes a clear report explaining exactly how to repeat the problem, so programmers can fix it.
每当出现问题，测试员都要写一份清楚的报告，准确说明如何重现这个问题，以便程序员修复。
Patience and attention to detail matter more than being a skilled player.
耐心和对细节的关注比游戏玩得好更重要。
For some people, the job is a first step into the games industry, leading to careers in design or programming.
对一些人来说，这份工作是进入游戏行业的第一步，之后可以走向设计或编程等职业。
q: What is a game tester's real task?
To find bugs before the public does
Why does a tester write a clear report?
So programmers can repeat and fix the problem
What matters most in this job, according to the passage?

title: The Open-Plan Office
photo: Open plan office / Office cubicles / Modern open office workspace
p: Walk into many modern offices and you will see long rows of desks with no walls between them.
走进许多现代办公室，你会看到一排排长长的办公桌，桌与桌之间没有任何隔断。
This open-plan design became popular because it saves space and, supposedly, encourages people to share ideas.
这种开放式设计之所以流行，是因为它节省空间，而且据说能鼓励人们交流想法。
Managers hoped that employees who could see each other would collaborate more naturally.
管理者希望，能看到彼此的员工会更自然地进行协作。
However, the reality is more complicated.
然而，现实要复杂得多。
Some studies have found that when companies moved to open offices, face-to-face conversation actually decreased while emails and messages increased.
一些研究发现，公司改用开放式办公室后，面对面的交谈反而减少了，而电子邮件和消息却增多了。
Feeling watched, many workers put on headphones to create their own private space.
由于感觉被人注视，很多员工戴上耳机，营造属于自己的私人空间。
Noise and interruptions can also make it difficult to concentrate on demanding tasks.
噪音和打扰也会让人难以专注于费脑力的工作。
As a result, many employers now mix open areas with quiet rooms and small booths for phone calls, giving staff a choice.
因此，许多雇主现在把开放区域与安静室和打电话用的小隔间结合起来，让员工有所选择。
q: Why did open-plan offices become popular?
They save space and were thought to encourage sharing ideas
They are quieter than other offices
What did some studies find after companies moved to open offices?
Mixing open areas with quiet rooms and booths

title: The Bystander Effect
photo: Crowd of people on city street / Pedestrians crossing busy street / People walking past
p: In 1964, the murder of a young woman named Kitty Genovese in New York shocked the United States.
1964年，一位名叫基蒂·吉诺维斯的年轻女子在纽约遇害，震惊全美。
Newspapers reported that dozens of neighbors had heard or seen the attack but done nothing, although later investigations showed that this account was greatly exaggerated.
报纸报道称，有几十位邻居听到或看到了袭击却无动于衷，尽管后来的调查表明，这种说法被严重夸大了。
Nevertheless, the story inspired two psychologists, John Darley and Bibb Latané, to ask why people sometimes fail to help in emergencies.
尽管如此，这个故事还是促使两位心理学家约翰·达利和比布·拉塔内去探究：为什么人们在紧急情况下有时不施以援手。
In a series of experiments, they found that people were less likely to respond to an emergency when others were present.
在一系列实验中，他们发现，当有其他人在场时，人们对紧急情况作出反应的可能性更低。
One explanation is the "diffusion of responsibility": each person assumes that someone else will act.
一种解释是“责任分散”：每个人都以为别人会采取行动。
Another is that people look to others to decide whether a situation is serious, and if everyone appears calm, they conclude that help is unnecessary.
另一种解释是，人们会参照他人来判断情况是否严重，如果每个人看起来都很平静，他们便断定无需帮忙。
Interestingly, more recent research analyzing real public conflicts recorded on camera suggests that bystanders intervene more often than the classic studies implied.
有意思的是，近来通过分析监控录像中真实公共冲突的研究表明，旁观者出手干预的频率比经典研究所暗示的要高。
Still, the practical lesson remains valuable: if you need help in a crowd, point to one specific person and ask them directly.
不过，其中的实用经验依然很有价值：如果你在人群中需要帮助，就指向某一个具体的人，直接向他求助。
q: What did later investigations show about the newspaper reports of the Genovese case?
They underestimated the number of witnesses
Each person assumes someone else will act
People are afraid of the attacker
Only experts are responsible for helping
What practical advice does the passage give?
Ask one specific person directly for help
Wait for the crowd to leave

title: Did a Machine Write This Essay?
zh: 这篇文章是机器写的吗？
photo: Student writing essay laptop / Artificial intelligence chatbot / University lecture hall laptops
p: Since AI chatbots that can produce fluent essays in seconds became widely available, teachers around the world have faced an uncomfortable question: how can they tell whether a student's work is really the student's own?
自从能在几秒内写出流畅文章的人工智能聊天机器人普及以来，世界各地的老师都面临一个令人尴尬的问题：如何判断学生的作业是否真正出自学生本人？
Software designed to detect machine-written text has proved unreliable, sometimes flagging honest students, particularly those writing in a second language.
专门用来检测机器生成文本的软件已被证明并不可靠，有时会错误标记诚实的学生，特别是用第二语言写作的学生。
Some institutions have responded by returning to handwritten exams and oral assessments, in which students must explain their reasoning face to face.
一些院校的应对办法是重新采用手写考试和口头评估，让学生当面解释自己的思路。
Others have taken the opposite approach, arguing that banning a tool students will use throughout their careers is neither realistic nor useful.
另一些院校则采取了相反的做法，他们认为，禁止一个学生在整个职业生涯中都会使用的工具既不现实，也没有意义。
These educators redesign assignments so that students must critique an AI-generated draft, check its facts or document how they used the tool.
这些教育者重新设计作业，要求学生评析人工智能生成的初稿、核查其中的事实，或记录自己是如何使用这个工具的。
Underlying the debate is a deeper question about the purpose of writing in education.
这场争论背后是一个更深层的问题：写作在教育中的目的究竟是什么。
If an essay is merely a product to be handed in, AI makes it trivially easy to obtain.
如果文章只是一件要上交的产品，那么人工智能让它变得唾手可得。
But if writing is a way of learning to think, then outsourcing it means skipping the very process that makes education valuable.
但如果写作是学习思考的一种方式，那么把它外包出去就意味着跳过了让教育有价值的那个过程本身。
w: 轻而易举地；微不足道地
q: What problem with AI-detection software does the passage mention?
It sometimes wrongly flags honest students
It is too expensive for schools
How do some educators redesign assignments?
Students critique AI drafts or check their facts
Students must write without computers at home
According to the final paragraph, why might outsourcing writing be harmful?
Writing is a way of learning to think

title: When Antibiotics Stop Working
photo: Penicillin mold petri dish / Antibiotic resistance bacteria culture / Alexander Fleming laboratory
p: When Alexander Fleming noticed in 1928 that a mold had killed bacteria in one of his petri dishes, he opened the door to one of medicine's greatest achievements.
1928年，亚历山大·弗莱明注意到一种霉菌杀死了他培养皿里的细菌，由此打开了医学史上最伟大成就之一的大门。
Penicillin and the antibiotics that followed turned once-deadly infections into routine illnesses.
青霉素以及随后出现的各种抗生素，把曾经致命的感染变成了寻常小病。
Yet in his Nobel Prize speech in 1945, Fleming warned that misuse of the drug could allow bacteria to become resistant.
然而，弗莱明在1945年的诺贝尔奖演讲中就警告说，滥用这种药物可能会让细菌产生耐药性。
His warning proved accurate.
他的警告后来被证明是准确的。
Whenever an antibiotic is used, the most vulnerable bacteria die first, while any that happen to survive can multiply and pass on their resistance.
每当使用抗生素时，最脆弱的细菌最先死亡，而碰巧存活下来的细菌则会繁殖并把耐药性传下去。
Taking antibiotics for viral infections such as colds, which they cannot treat, or stopping a course early, gives this process more opportunities.
用抗生素治疗它们根本治不了的病毒感染（如感冒），或者提前停药，都为这一过程提供了更多机会。
The heavy use of antibiotics in farm animals adds to the problem.
在养殖动物身上大量使用抗生素更是加剧了这一问题。
The World Health Organization regards antimicrobial resistance as one of the top global threats to public health.
世界卫生组织将抗微生物药物耐药性视为全球公共卫生面临的最大威胁之一。
Solutions include developing new drugs, improving hygiene and vaccination to prevent infections in the first place, and prescribing antibiotics only when they are genuinely needed.
解决办法包括研发新药、改善卫生条件和推广疫苗接种以从源头上预防感染，以及仅在真正需要时才开具抗生素。
q: What did Fleming warn about in 1945?
Why is taking antibiotics for a cold a problem?
They cannot treat viral infections and encourage resistance
It makes the cold last forever
Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a solution?
Using more antibiotics in farm animals

title: Four Days a Week?
photo: Empty office Friday / Calendar work week / Office workers leaving work
p: The idea of a five-day, forty-hour working week is so familiar that it seems almost natural, yet it is a relatively recent invention.
每周工作五天、四十小时的观念如此熟悉，以至于看起来几乎是天经地义的，但它其实是相对较新的发明。
In the 1920s, the American industrialist Henry Ford adopted it in his factories, partly in the belief that workers with more leisure time would also buy more goods.
二十世纪二十年代，美国实业家亨利·福特在他的工厂里采用了这一制度，部分原因是他相信，有更多闲暇时间的工人也会购买更多商品。
Today, some companies are experimenting with a further step: a four-day week without a cut in pay.
如今，一些公司正在尝试更进一步：每周工作四天，而工资不减。

In trials in several countries, including a large pilot in the UK in 2022, many participating employers reported that productivity held steady while staff felt less stressed and were less likely to quit.
在包括2022年英国一项大型试点在内的多个国家的试验中，许多参与的雇主表示，生产率保持稳定，而员工的压力减轻，离职意愿也降低了。
The secret, supporters say, is cutting unnecessary meetings and distractions rather than simply squeezing five days of work into four.
支持者说，秘诀在于砍掉不必要的会议和干扰，而不是简单地把五天的工作塞进四天。
Skeptics point out that the companies volunteering for such trials may be those best suited to them.
怀疑者指出，自愿参加这类试验的公司可能本来就是最适合这种模式的公司。
It is far from clear how a shorter week would work for hospitals, schools or shops that must stay open, and some employees find longer working days exhausting.
对于必须保持开放的医院、学校或商店来说，缩短工作周如何实施还远不清楚，而且一些员工觉得更长的工作日令人筋疲力尽。
q: Why did Henry Ford partly support a shorter week?
He believed workers with more leisure would buy more goods
He wanted to close his factories
Workers refused to work on Saturdays
According to supporters, what is the secret to a successful four-day week?
Companies that volunteer may be the ones best suited to it
Workers will earn too much money

title: The Gentle Power of the Nudge
photo: Cafeteria food display / Fruit at checkout counter / Stairs and escalator choice
p: Traditional economics assumed that people make rational decisions by carefully weighing costs and benefits.
传统经济学假定，人们会通过仔细权衡成本和收益来做出理性的决定。
Behavioral economists, however, have shown that our choices are strongly influenced by how options are presented.
然而，行为经济学家已经证明，我们的选择在很大程度上受到选项呈现方式的影响。
In their 2008 book Nudge, Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein argued that governments and organizations could use this insight to help people make better decisions without restricting their freedom.
理查德·塞勒和卡斯·桑斯坦在2008年出版的《助推》一书中提出，政府和组织可以利用这一洞见，在不限制人们自由的前提下帮助他们做出更好的决定。
Thaler later received the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2017.
塞勒后来于2017年获得了诺贝尔经济学奖。
A classic example is the power of defaults.
一个经典的例子是默认选项的力量。
When employees are automatically enrolled in a retirement savings plan and must actively choose to leave it, far more of them end up saving than when they must actively sign up.
如果员工被自动加入退休储蓄计划，必须主动选择才能退出，那么最终存钱的人数会比必须主动报名时多得多。
Similarly, placing fruit at eye level in a cafeteria can encourage healthier eating without banning anything.
同样，在食堂里把水果放在与视线齐平的位置，可以在不禁止任何东西的情况下鼓励更健康的饮食。
Critics worry that nudges can be manipulative, especially when companies use the same techniques to push customers toward choices that benefit the company rather than the customer.
批评者担心助推可能带有操纵性，尤其是当企业用同样的手段把顾客推向有利于企业而非顾客的选择时。
Supporters respond that every choice is presented in some way, so the real question is whether the design serves people's own interests.
支持者回应说，任何选择都必然以某种方式呈现，所以真正的问题在于这种设计是否符合人们自身的利益。
q: People make rational decisions by weighing costs and benefits
People's choices depend on how options are presented
Why do more employees save when enrolled automatically?
Because of the power of defaults
Because saving is required by law
Because they read the plan carefully
What is the critics' main concern about nudges?

title: Fast Fashion's Hidden Costs
photo: Clothing store racks / Textile waste pile / Second-hand clothes market
p: Not long ago, most clothing brands released new collections a few times a year.
不久以前，大多数服装品牌一年只推出几次新系列。
Today, so-called fast fashion companies can move a design from the drawing board to the store in a matter of weeks, offering cheap, trendy clothes that many shoppers wear only a handful of times.
如今，所谓的快时尚公司能在短短几周内把一个设计从画板送进门店，提供廉价而时髦的衣服，而很多购物者只穿几次就不穿了。
The low price tag, however, conceals considerable costs.
然而，低廉的价签背后隐藏着相当大的代价。
Growing cotton requires large amounts of water, and dyeing fabric can pollute rivers when factories release untreated wastewater.
种植棉花需要大量的水，而如果工厂排放未经处理的废水，布料染色还可能污染河流。
Many cheap garments are made from polyester, a plastic-based material that sheds tiny fibers when washed.
许多廉价服装由涤纶制成，这是一种以塑料为原料的材料，洗涤时会脱落微小的纤维。
The human cost drew worldwide attention in 2013, when the Rana Plaza building in Bangladesh, which housed several garment factories, collapsed and killed more than a thousand workers.
2013年，孟加拉国容纳了数家服装厂的拉纳广场大楼倒塌，造成一千多名工人死亡，其中的人力代价由此引起全世界关注。
In response, some consumers are buying second-hand, repairing clothes or simply buying less.
作为回应，一些消费者开始购买二手衣物、修补衣服，或者干脆少买。
Some brands now offer repair services or take back old clothes, although critics warn that such schemes can be little more than marketing unless overall production falls.
一些品牌现在提供修补服务或回收旧衣，不过批评者警告说，除非总产量下降，否则这类计划可能只不过是营销手段而已。
q: What is typical of fast fashion companies?
They move designs to stores within weeks
They release one collection every few years
They make clothes to last a lifetime
What problem with polyester does the passage mention?
It sheds tiny fibers when washed
It needs huge amounts of water to grow
Why are critics skeptical of take-back schemes?
They may be just marketing unless overall production falls
They are illegal in many countries

title: Inside the Filter Bubble
photo: Social media feed smartphone / Person scrolling phone / News app on smartphone
p: Every time you like a post, watch a video to the end or click on a headline, you are teaching an algorithm what you prefer.
每当你点赞一条帖子、看完一个视频或点开一条新闻标题，你都在教算法了解你的喜好。
Social media platforms and video sites use this information to recommend more content you are likely to enjoy, which keeps you on the platform longer.
社交媒体平台和视频网站利用这些信息，向你推荐更多你可能喜欢的内容，从而让你在平台上停留更久。
In 2011, the internet activist Eli Pariser coined the term "filter bubble" to describe a possible side effect of this personalization.
2011年，网络活动人士伊莱·帕里泽创造了“过滤气泡”一词，用来描述这种个性化推荐可能带来的副作用。
If we mainly see information that matches our existing views, he argued, we may gradually lose contact with other perspectives and become more certain that we are right.
他认为，如果我们看到的主要是与自己既有观点相符的信息，我们可能会逐渐与其他视角失去接触，并变得更加确信自己是对的。
Researchers continue to debate how strong this effect really is.
研究人员对于这种效应到底有多强仍有争议。
Some studies suggest that many people still encounter a range of viewpoints online, and that our own choices about whom to follow may matter as much as any algorithm.
一些研究表明，很多人在网上仍会接触到各种不同的观点，而我们自己选择关注谁，可能与任何算法一样重要。
Even so, the concept has encouraged a healthy habit: deliberately seeking out reliable sources that challenge, rather than simply confirm, what we already believe.
即便如此，这一概念还是促成了一个健康的习惯：有意识地寻找那些挑战而不是单纯印证我们已有观念的可靠信息来源。
q: Why do platforms recommend content you are likely to enjoy?
To keep you on the platform longer
Mainly seeing information that matches your existing views
A way to clean your phone screen
A type of social media platform
Our own choices of whom to follow may matter as much as algorithms
Filter bubbles do not exist at all

title: The Puzzle of the Placebo
photo: Pills and capsules / Clinical trial medicine / Doctor patient consultation
p: A placebo is a treatment with no active ingredient, such as a sugar pill, yet patients who take one sometimes report genuine improvement.
安慰剂是一种不含有效成分的治疗手段，比如糖丸，然而服用它的病人有时会报告病情确实有所好转。
This placebo effect is especially noticeable for symptoms such as pain, nausea and fatigue, which are strongly shaped by the brain's expectations.
这种安慰剂效应在疼痛、恶心和疲劳等症状上尤为明显，因为这些症状在很大程度上受大脑预期的影响。
Because of it, new medicines are usually tested in randomized, double-blind trials.
正因如此，新药通常要经过随机双盲试验的检验。
One group receives the real drug and another receives an identical-looking placebo, and neither the patients nor the researchers know who received which until the end.
一组服用真药，另一组服用外观相同的安慰剂，直到试验结束，病人和研究人员都不知道谁服用的是哪一种。
A drug is considered effective only if it performs clearly better than the placebo.
只有当药物的效果明显好于安慰剂时，它才被认为是有效的。
Surprisingly, some studies have found that placebos can help even when patients are told openly that the pills contain nothing active.
令人惊讶的是，一些研究发现，即使明确告诉病人药片里不含任何有效成分，安慰剂仍然可能起作用。
Researchers believe the ritual of care, including a confident doctor, a clear explanation and the act of taking medicine, may trigger the body's own pain-relieving systems.
研究人员认为，包括一位自信的医生、清楚的解释以及服药这一行为在内的整个关怀仪式，可能会激活人体自身的镇痛系统。
Placebos cannot shrink tumors or cure infections, but they remind us that the relationship between mind and body is more intricate than we once thought.
安慰剂无法让肿瘤缩小或治愈感染，但它们提醒我们，身心之间的关系比我们曾经以为的要复杂得多。
q: For which kind of symptoms is the placebo effect especially noticeable?
In a double-blind trial, who knows which patients receive the real drug?
No one, until the end of the trial
Placebos can help even when patients know they are placebos
Placebos work better than all real drugs
